newsitem.title: POLAND: Philip Morris to boost Polish investment.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris to boost Polish investment.

text.p: Philip Morris said on Monday it wanted to increase investment at its cigarette-producing plant in southern Poland to more than $200 million from earlier planned $145 million.

"When we purchased the Krakow plant...our investment commitment was $145 million over the next three years. We now project the investment to exeed $200 million," the plant's president Andre Calanzopoulos told a news conference.

Early last year, Philip Morris agreed to pay $372 million for a controlling stake in the country's biggest cigarette producer Zaklady Przemyslu Tytoniowego Krakow SA, which has a 30 percent share of Poland's lucrative tobacco market.
Calanzopoulos said he was satisfied with the Polish market even though officially registered cigarette consumption dropped last year by about seven percent to 90 billion.
Even if the Polish cigarette market continues to fall, Philip Morris will try to boost sales by gaining market share at the expense of its rivals, he said.
But Calanzopoulos said real consumption of cigarettes last year was likely to have been higher as it was fed by cross-boder smuggling.
The smuggling was likely to increase if the finance ministry continued to boost the excise tax on tobacco products, he said.
He said, without giving details, that the Krakow plant's net profit fell last year compared with 1995 while revenues increased.
"This is normal in the first or second year after an acquisition...due to investment," he said.
Calanzopoulos also criticised a recent decision by the lower house of parliament to go ahead with large new health warnings on cigarette packs.
Under the law, which may still be changed by the Senate, a cigarette pack will have to carry warnings over at least 30 percent of each large side of a pack from the end of 1997.
Calanzopoulos said that after Poland joined the European Union foreign products, carrying much smaller warnings, would have an advantage over locally produced ones.
